title: YouCoded plan — active work and private planning

steps.headline: 1. See current work, the next decision and recent progress at a glance.
steps.changed: Nested cards became a work list with clear Now and Next groups, owners, next steps and an attention column.
steps.notice: You can find what needs action without opening each planning document.
steps.risk: All records, people, dates and shipping statuses are fictional design data, not claims about repository progress.

steps.headline: 2. Edit a work item through named fields rather than rewriting its plan.
steps.changed: Title, status, timing, owner, source and next step have separate fields with Save and Cancel.
steps.notice: A saved draft updates the private overview; detailed documents remain linked.
steps.risk: Edits live only in the sandbox frame and reset when it reloads; no files or backend records are written.

steps.headline: 3. Follow dated reports back to their author and source.
steps.changed: History includes a build report, planning change, community issue and private request, each with a date and reporter.
steps.notice: Issue discussion remains in GitHub; private conversation requests are not automatically public reports.
steps.risk: Reports and issues are fictional; source buttons reveal local sample text rather than opening real documents or GitHub.

steps.headline: 4. Compare the public summary before approving each update.
steps.changed: Published and proposed text appear side by side, with a second confirmation before approval.
steps.notice: Only the listed summaries are reviewed; private notes and full documents stay out of the public view.
steps.risk: Approval changes local interface state only: there is no publication, network request or GitHub write.

steps.headline: 5. See the folder, computer and separate read, write and network permissions.
steps.changed: The remembered grant names its host and folder, offers Revoke, and keeps GitHub network access separate.
steps.notice: Choosing a folder shows an explicit confirmation with your read and write choices.
steps.risk: Folder choices, grants and revocation are interface demonstrations only; no actual permission or file access changes.

steps.headline: 6. Stop and review when the host, source or saved draft changes.
steps.changed: Dedicated states show a changed host, unavailable source history and competing next-step values.
steps.notice: A host grant cannot silently transfer to another computer; draft choices are shown before replacing a value.
steps.risk: These are fixture-only exception states, not real failure detection; conflict selection does not reconcile files.

steps.headline: 7. Keep long-term direction separate from scheduled work.
steps.changed: Vision explains ownership, provider choice and reusable tools, with device host selection marked as an open decision.
steps.notice: Future direction remains visible without making unscheduled ideas look like current commitments.
steps.risk: This direction is candidate copy; it is not a technical architecture or implementation promise.
